tldr: Headlines across all 11 buckets frame the Macklemore/Ed Sheeran incident through three diverging lenses. Most international outlets (European, Canadian, Latin American, UK, Indian) neutrally foreground Macklemore's 'pro-Palestinian remarks' as the stated reason for removal. US conservative outlets (Breitbart, Daily Wire) and Germany's Bild inject moral-condemnation language absent elsewhere — casting the same speech as 'unhinged anti-Israel tirades,' a 'pro-Islamic terrorist rant,' or 'Israel-hate.' Middle East Eye and Haaretz stand apart by foregrounding the mechanism: a billionaire's organised pressure campaign. Pakistan's Geo News alone applies a positive moral frame, describing Macklemore's stance as a 'bold move.'

single_outlet_findings.finding: Headlines characterise Macklemore's speech as a 'Pro-Islamic Terrorist Rant' and his response as 'blaming' a Jewish owner — the most extreme editorial characterisation in the corpus.
Leads with 'Rapper verbreitet Israel-Hass' (rapper spreads Israel-hate), the only non-US outlet to use moral-condemnation framing equivalent to right-wing American coverage.

bottom_line: The headline layer divides sharply by political culture: international and wire outlets report Macklemore's removal as a factual consequence of pro-Palestinian speech; US conservative and German tabloid outlets reframe that speech as 'hate' or 'terrorism-adjacent'; Middle East Eye and Haaretz alone name Robert Kraft's billionaire pressure campaign as the operative mechanism, turning a music-tour story into one about organised political suppression.
